extraction.pages_processed: Whole webpage text read in full (opening paragraphs and sections Attributes of Vulnerability, Existing Efforts, Filling the Gaps)
extraction.notes: HTML snapshot of the RUSI commentary by James Osborne and Joseph Jarnecki (10 August 2023), read in full. The text file has no pages; items under a section heading cite the section (page left empty) and the snapshot file; items from the opening paragraphs, which have no heading, cite text page 1 with the section given as 'Opening paragraphs (no heading)'. The commentary uses 'cyber defence' broadly for national cyber security. Scope applied: security of networks and information systems (TECH-CYBER) is in scope; cybercrime enforcement, military cyber defence and disinformation are out. Left out: the description of Russian information operations, hack-and-leak campaigns as part of wider hostile activity and the resignation of the former Prime Minister (disinformation and political context), except one item on attacks that disrupted state services, flagged theme_doubtful; the 300% increase in cyber operations against NATO countries (not about Moldova); EU4Digital support for legislation under the Budapest Convention on Cybercrime (cybercrime, R21); the expected activities of the Cyber Rapid Response Team (speculative, 'can be expected'); the sentence that international support shows an acknowledgement that cyber defence is best built before an incident (an interpretation of partners' views); the Ukraine example as such (other country's experience); author and page furniture. The two pull quotes repeat sentences of the running text and are not extracted again. Doubtful for the analyst (theme_doubtful): the Cyber Rapid Response Team under PESCO, the 'hunt forward' operations modelled on US Cyber Command, fast-tracked participation in NATO CCDCOE exercises, the programme's lack of operational support for cyber defence, insider threats and the attacks framed as information operations; all concern the security of Moldovan networks but sit close to the military and disinformation line. Second-pass check (PC-05) by checker-GOV8b on 5 November 2026: 2 items added (review/RUN-2026-02/second_pass/MDA-RES-2023-001.csv).

items.stated_text: Efforts by Moldova’s government and international actors have begun to build the country’s cyber capacity. Nonetheless, several factors mean Moldova remains vulnerable to cyber operations.
items.summary: Government and international efforts have begun to build Moldova's cyber capacity, but the country remains vulnerable to cyber operations.

items.stated_text: It has low government revenue compared with its European peers and several pressing priorities for state expenditure. Socio-economic challenges including a contracting population, an over-reliance on remittances and inflation detract from the government’s ability to spend on cyber security.
items.summary: Low revenue, competing priorities and socio-economic challenges limit the government's ability to spend on cyber security.

items.stated_text: As demonstrated by the large-scale cyber incidents suffered by Albania and Costa Rica , small states which are unable or choose not to spend on cyber security are highly vulnerable to significant impact.
items.summary: Incidents in Albania and Costa Rica show that small states that do not spend on cyber security are highly vulnerable.
items.extraction_note: Stated lesson drawn from other countries' experience and applied to Moldova's situation in the same paragraph. Repeated as a pull quote, not extracted again.

items.stated_text: While accusations have primarily been levelled within the political sphere , infiltration also impacts national cyber security. An insider could, for instance, grant hostile actors access to critical systems.
